confirmed.title: Back link is an open redirect: dot segments turn a validated ref into //host
confirmed.detail: refPathOf checks `s.startsWith("//")` on the raw input and then returns `new URL(s, base).pathname`, but the WHATWG parser collapses dot segments AFTER that check. Verified with node: `/..//evil.com`, `/.//evil.com` and `/a/..//evil.com` all return the pathname `//evil.com`. That value passes every guard (starts with `/`, no whitespace, no quotes, no backslash) and reaches line 47 as `<Link href="//evil.com">`. A protocol-relative href is not local to Next (isLocalURL resolves it to origin https://evil.com), so the click falls through to the browser and lands on https://evil.com. `miltonly.com/book?ref=/..//evil.com` is therefore a phishing link on a first-party domain whose anchor text says "Back to the page you were on". The form sends the same `//evil.com` as `ref`; ingest.ts:182 drops it on its own `//` check, so the Lead row is unaffected. The link is the defect.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Validate the normalized output, not the input: `const p = new URL(s, "https://miltonly.invalid").pathname; return p.startsWith("/") && !p.startsWith("//") ? p : null;`. Optionally also reject any `/./` or `/../` segment before parsing. Add the three inputs above as negative cases in scripts/test-lead-forms.ts or a small page test.
